value.rationale: At fixed physically prescribed three-tap magnitudes, the exact best mean-square spectral spread and all optimizing phases and channel gaps form a complete natural finite harmonic-frame design problem. The exact nonnegative deficit quantifies spectral design rigidity and the even-order threshold beta=cos(pi/N) proves a real amplitude-driven change of optimum. Identical-magnitude windows can change from a non-tight optimum 44N/9 to an exactly tight system 4N solely by phase design. This is more informative than the universal potential bound or merely verifying a given frame.
